title: Visitor Pattern
concept: The Visitor pattern separates operations from the objects they operate on — adding new operations to complex object structures without modifying the objects.
why: When you have a complex type hierarchy (like AST nodes), adding new operations requires modifying every subtype. Visitor lets you add operations externally.
tips: Use Visitor when you add many operations to a fixed set of types
The Visitor interface should have one method per concrete type in the hierarchy
Visitors are pure functions — they transform data, not modify it
For small, stable type hierarchies, match expressions are simpler than Visitor
common_mistakes: Using Visitor when the type hierarchy changes frequently — adding types requires updating ALL visitors
Making visitors stateful — they should be stateless computation units
Visitors that return void — prefer returning a value to enable composition and testing
